subject: PriorityBank: KV-cache backlog causing 5xx/latency spike — urgent
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@prioritybank.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: PriorityBank SRE <sre@prioritybank.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden 5xx wave + latency — appears tied to KV cache backlog

Hi Grace,

We started seeing a 5xx spike and 2–3x p95 latency increase around 08:45 PT this morning for our inference routes that hit your dedicated pool. Ops dug in and observed a growing KV-cache backlog — requests are queuing and then timeouting with 503s. Attached is a trimmed log sample and a chart with queue depth.

This is impacting live payments (timeout -> retries -> duplicate attempts). We flagged a P1. Can Redwood confirm whether autoscaling for the dedicated pool is behaving as expected and whether any rollout or kernel changes happened in the 08:00–09:00 window?

PriorityBank impact: ~30% failure rate on core routes; our fraud flows are degraded. We need a short-term mitigation and an ETA for a fix.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Director, Platform Reliability
PriorityBank

Attachment: prioritybank-kvcache-sample-logs.txt (plain text, 48KB)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@prioritybank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden 5xx wave + latency — appears tied to KV cache backlog

Alice — thanks for the quick heads-up and the log sample.

Short answer: we see the same signal in internal telemetry for the dedicated pool assigned to PriorityBank. Initial triage shows:
- Rapid growth of KV cache miss/eviction churn around 08:40.
- Autoscaler did attempt a scale-up but paired instances are hitting persistent hot-spotting on a subset of GPUs (inefficient shard placement).
- No model rollout or kernel change recorded in the window.

Immediate plan (we're kicking this off now):
1) Ops: force an explicit scale and re-balance KV shard placement to reduce hot spots (15–30m).
2) Mitigation: apply a temporary routing rule to divert non-critical traffic to a fallback quantized model variant with lower memory pressure.
3) Engineering: enable an expedited flushing policy for stale KV entries to clear backlog fast (if safe).

I'll loop in David for executive visibility and Marissa to coordinate customer comms. We will update every 30 minutes until resolved.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

We are on it — infra is performing the re-shard and live migration now. Preliminary findings: one host (gpu-7b-12) has an OS-level process leak causing slower KV response; that made shard placement imbalance obvious. Actions in flight:
- Live migrate the two hottest shards off gpu-7b-12 (ETA 20m).
- Temporarily bump PriorityBank pool's memory headroom + add a cache-throttling guard (ETA 10m, requires ops approval).
- Add an emergency routing rule to send low-priority traffic to a fallback endpoint (implemented at the router layer, ETA 15m).

I will publish a timeline to JIRA INF-4821 and post updates. If the live migration doesn't bring latency back under control, we will request burst GPU capacity.

— Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alice — quick operational update and commitments:

What's fixed (as of 16:30 PT):
- KV shard migration completed; queue depth dropped by ~85%.
- Hot host (gpu-7b-12) removed from the pool for post-mortem; no kernel or model rollout detected.
- Temporary routing to fallback model is live — non-critical routes now stable.

Next steps and ask of PriorityBank SRE:
- We want your SRE to validate transaction flows for the next 2 hours while we monitor; please confirm previous replay tests are safe to run.
- We'll run a controlled warm-up to rebuild cold KV entries slowly (avoids sudden burst).
- We will share a post-incident report and a remediation plan by EOD Monday covering: shard placement improvements, autoscaler tuning, and a pre-authorized burst capacity play for payment-critical windows.

Attachments: pending-action-matrix.xlsx (contains proposed owner/timeline for each remediation step).

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you appraised every 30 minutes for the next 2 hours.
